name: ghidra
description: Reverse engineering via Ghidra CLI (akiselev/ghidra-cli) — headless analysis, decompilation, function/symbol/type editing, cross-refs, search, patching, and scripting from the terminal.
prerequisites: Full JDK, not a JRE (21 for Ghidra 12.x, 17+ for older)
Ghidra 11+ install (or run `ghidra setup` after install)

install.notes: ghidra-cli is a Rust CLI not yet published to crates.io; install from the GitHub source. Requires a full JDK (21 for Ghidra 12.x) and a Ghidra 11+ install; the CLI auto-selects the JDK (override with --java-home or GHIDRA_CLI_JAVA_HOME). After install, run `ghidra setup` to auto-download Ghidra, or set GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR / `ghidra config set ghidra_install_dir <path>`.

integration_test.description: Verifies CLI sees the Ghidra install, selects a full JDK, and compiles the bridge script.

post_install_hints: Install a full JDK 21 (Ghidra 12.x) if not present (Windows: `winget install --id Microsoft.OpenJDK.21 -e --source winget`; macOS: `brew install openjdk@21`; Linux: `sudo apt install openjdk-21-jdk`).
Install Ghidra: either run `ghidra setup` to auto-download, or download from https://ghidra-sre.org and set GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR (or `ghidra config set ghidra_install_dir <path>`).
Verify with `ghidra doctor` — it checks the Ghidra install, selects a JDK, compiles the bridge script, and shows the project directory.
